title: The four modals that still let Tab wander onto the page behind them now keep it inside

source.ref: SCAN-1225 follow-up, 2026-11-16: the four modals that row's closing note lists as having no Tab trap at all.

detail:
SCAN-1225 moved nine hand-rolled modals onto the kit focus trap (components/ui/use-dialog-focus-trap, PR #5029) and named four true modals that had no Tab trap: with one open, Tab walked out onto the page behind it. This row puts those four on the same hook. Markup, classes, labels and how each opens and closes are unchanged.

1. components/layout/marketing-mobile-menu.tsx (the public phone menu, aria-modal). It already focused Close on open, closed on Escape and returned focus to the Open menu button; it gains the Tab trap. Its own effect is kept and its cleanup runs after the hook's, so focus still returns to the Open menu button where a tap never focused it (Safari).
2. components/layout/admin-bar/admin-bar.tsx (the phone Page settings sheet, aria-modal, portaled over the whole screen). It had Escape and nothing else: no first focus, no trap, no focus return. It gains all three. First focus goes to Close, the same target the desktop bar uses, unless the body already focused a requested app entry. That is set before the hook runs because the hook's default is the first focusable, which is the backdrop button, and the next is the search field, which would raise the keyboard on a phone. SCAN-1225 marked this one as needing a design call on first focus; Close was chosen because the desktop bar already does it. Say so if another target is wanted.
3. components/frequency/site/pages/themes/kit-showcase/kit-showcase-view.tsx (the full-size view on /themes, aria-modal). It had Escape only. It gains first focus (the first surface tab), the Tab trap and focus return to the tile that opened it. The hook is called in the view file, two lines, because that file writes the dialog element; Escape and the backdrop tap stay in use-kit-showcase.ts.
4. components/frequency/admin/pages/moderation/report-queue.tsx (the inline role=alertdialog confirm under a report). It had no focus handling at all. The confirm is now its own small component, same markup and classes, with the trap, focus return to the button that opened it, first focus on Keep (the safe answer, not the destructive first button) and Escape answering Keep. Escape is new behaviour here: a trapped prompt needs a keyboard way out.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER. The four SCAN-1225 lists as trapping Tab with their own code are untouched: builder/command/command-bar and builder/legacy/update-layouts-sheet (each pinned by a probe or test), frequency/members/shell/header and frequency/site/shell/site-header. marketing-mobile-menu is statically reachable from the member layout (through components/layout/viewer-chrome.tsx), so the hook (878 bytes minified) is now in the member shell's first load and, through components/layout/marketing-header.tsx, in the front door's; SCAN-1225 held this file back for the shell's sake. NOT MEASURED: check:shell-weight runs only on a real build, and a draft PR gets no preview build. The last production build on main (7f157ed4c, 2026-11-16) printed 1076 KB of 1100 for the member shell and 446 KB of 450 for the front door, so the front door had about 4 KB left before this change. Get a preview build's reading before this merges; if the front door goes over, take the phone menu back out of this change and leave the other three. Not verified in a browser: jsdom reports no client rects, so the hook's Tab wrap cannot be driven in the unit tests here.

All four are on the kit hook and the probe passes. The shell weight reading is still owed: see NOT MEASURED above.

verify.note: For each of the four files, comments stripped: the kit hook is imported, called with a ref, and that ref is on the element carrying aria-modal="true" or role="alertdialog". Fails on the tree before this row, where none of the four imports the hook.
